summary:
I'll pull concrete details from the notes and write the dashboard section.

I've been building out fleet monitoring for the home server rack — four boxes (a desktop AI server, three headless machines) reporting over SSH every 30 seconds into a SQLite time series, with a retention ladder that keeps raw data for a week, 5-minute rollups for 90 days, then hourly for a year, and never throws away the min/max so a spike doesn't get averaged into invisibility. I added power monitoring on top of it recently: four months of real wattage samples on the AI box (mean 179W, ~131 kWh a month) confirmed a back-of-envelope estimate I'd made earlier, which was satisfying in a boring way. The harder part was resisting the urge to reach for Prometheus or Grafana once the thing already did what I needed — I'd actually recommended Prometheus at one point before remembering I'd already built the alternative.

On TheLongRest, my D&D campaign manager, I found and closed an API route that returned an entire database row instead of a curated subset — it was shipping encrypted integration tokens and every member's email address to anyone in the campaign, not just the DM. Rather than patch that one endpoint, I pulled the fix into a shared select-only helper and added a test that deep-scans the JSON response for anything that looks like a secret key, so the same mistake can't recur somewhere else. I also shipped a photo-import feature for adventure content, which surfaced a fun constraint: the vision model refuses to transcribe copyrighted published text outright, so the feature works for homebrew notes and stat blocks but sends people back to copy-paste for anything from a published book.

The other big chunk of recent work was infrastructure debugging rather than features. A stale DNS wildcard on one of my servers was silently resolving every failed lookup to the wrong machine, which made an unrelated automated agent falsely believe it had fixed a networking problem it hadn't touched — that one taught me to verify an agent's account of what it did against the actual system state (docker inspect, config diffs) rather than trust the summary. Separately, a Python audio library that couldn't recover from a dropped connection ran silently broken for a week and generated 180,000 error log lines before I noticed, so I wrote a small watchdog that restarts the service and throttles its own alerts instead of flooding me.

highlights.oneLiner: Serializes one shared GPU across local models; rebuilt after a half-deployed change.
Local agent on a native service, plus a watchdog for a dead Slack socket.
Site and dashboard tile that names recent work from an allowlist.
Image backend that takes a GPU lease before rendering.
